questions.question: A pencil starts at 0 cm on a ruler and ends at 5 cm. How many centimetres long is it?
questions.explain: The pencil goes from 0 to 5, so it is 5 cm long. Counting the 6 marks on the ruler is a common mix-up.

questions.question: A ruler shows a crayon from 0 cm to 7 cm. How long is the crayon?
questions.explain: It goes from 0 to 7, so the length is 7 cm. Counting the 8 marks gives one too many.

questions.question: A pencil starts at 2 cm on a ruler and ends at 8 cm. How long is it?
questions.explain: Subtract the start from the end: 8 minus 2 is 6 cm. The trap is just reading the 8 at the end.

questions.question: A stick starts at 2 cm and ends at 7 cm on a ruler. How many centimetres long is the stick?
questions.explain: Take the end minus the start: 7 minus 2 is 5 cm. Reading only the 7 at the end is the most common slip.

questions.question: Ben puts a pencil on the ruler on his desk. One end is at 2 cm and the other end is at 9 cm. How long is the pencil?
questions.explain: The length is the end minus the start: 9 minus 2 equals 7 cm. Reading only the 9 at the end is the trap.

questions.question: Mia measures a crayon on her desk ruler. One end lines up with 3 cm and the other with 9 cm. How long is the crayon?
questions.explain: Subtract the start from the end: 9 minus 3 is 6 cm. Counting the 7 marks from 3 to 9 gives one too many.

questions.question: Tom finds a worm and measures it with a ruler. The head is at 4 cm and the tail is at 8 cm. How long is the worm?
questions.explain: The length is 8 minus 4, which is 4 cm. The trap is just reading the 8 at the tail.

questions.question: Sara places a craft stick on the ruler. One end is at 4 cm and the other end is at 9 cm. How many centimetres is the stick?
questions.explain: The length is 9 minus 4, which is 5 cm. Counting the 6 marks from 4 to 9 gives one too many.

questions.question: A pencil is on the ruler. One end is at 3 cm and the pencil is 4 cm long. Where does the other end line up?
questions.explain: Add the length to the start: 3 plus 4 is 7 cm. Counting 4 marks from 3 lands on 6, which is one short.

questions.question: An eraser is on the ruler. One end is at 3 cm. The eraser is 5 cm long. Where is the other end?
questions.explain: Add the length to the start: 3 plus 5 is 8 cm. Counting 5 marks from 3 lands on 7, which is one short.

questions.question: Sara puts a book on the ruler. The left edge is at 1 cm and the right edge is at 7 cm. She slides the book so the left edge is now at 3 cm. Where is the right edge now?
questions.explain: First find the length: 7 minus 1 is 6 cm. Then add that to the new start: 3 plus 6 is 9 cm. The trap is reading the old end.

questions.question: Mia measures from 3 cm to 9 cm on a ruler. She says the length is 9 cm. What did Mia do wrong?
options: She used the start mark as the length.
She mixed up centimetres and metres.
She counted the marks, not the spaces.
She read only the end, not the start.
questions.explain: The length is 9 minus 3, which is 6 cm. Mia just read the 9 at the end and forgot to take away the 3 at the start.
